meta_description: Harvest logistics on a field-to-silo twin — logistics cost down 14% and moisture-driven quality losses down 29%

blocks.x: Harvest logistics on a field-to-silo twin, logistics cost down 14% and moisture-driven quality losses down 29%
Identity withheld, a grain cooperative whose harvest moved on habit and whose silos received whatever the roads delivered. Figures are the client's own, shared with permission.

The baseline season measured the habit: trucks queuing 4.2 hours at peak intake, moisture variability adding quality discounts at delivery, and logistics cost per ton rising while members' patience fell.
Field readiness, weather windows and silo capacity were known to three different coordinators who never shared a schedule. The harvest was a negotiation conducted by phone.

We built the field-to-silo twin: moisture and readiness signals per field zone, weather windows joined to harvest progress, silo intake capacity modeled live, truck scheduling optimized against the whole chain with dispatchers approving exceptions, and member-facing windows published from the same model. The phone negotiation became a schedule everyone reads.
